nodes.name: Reference asset type
nodes.question: What does the asset reference to maintain a stable value?

nodes.name: Issuer identifiability
nodes.question: Is there an identifiable person or entity that issues the crypto-asset?

nodes.name: Crypto-asset definitional criteria
nodes.question: Does the digital item meet the criteria to count as a crypto-asset, digital asset or virtual asset?

nodes.name: Fungibility
nodes.question: Is the crypto-asset fungible, i.e. interchangeable with other units of the same asset?

nodes.name: Economic function of the asset
nodes.question: What is the economic purpose the asset serves: payment, investment, access to a service, or governance?

nodes.name: Native asset versus token standard
nodes.question: Is the crypto-asset native to its own blockchain or a token issued under a smart-contract standard on another chain?

nodes.name: Tokenisation form
nodes.question: Is the asset a token that represents ownership or rights in an off-chain or other asset?

nodes.name: Wrapped / cross-chain representation
nodes.question: Is the crypto-asset a representation of another asset locked on a different chain or in custody?

nodes.name: Source of yield
nodes.question: From what economic activity or protocol mechanism does the holder's return derive?

nodes.name: Yield distribution mechanism
nodes.question: How is yield delivered to holders: by increasing balance, redemption ratio, price, or another asset?

nodes.name: Redemption mechanism
nodes.question: How and by whom can the holder convert the crypto-asset back into its reference asset?

nodes.name: Form of holder claim
nodes.question: Does the holder hold a contractual claim against an issuer, a property-type interest in a reserve pool, or no claim?

nodes.name: Centralisation of control
nodes.question: Who controls the critical resources of the asset (governance, minting, yield, redemption), and is that control concentrated in one entity?

nodes.name: Decentralised system certification
nodes.question: Does the blockchain system meet the statutory conditions to be treated as a decentralised system or mature blockchain system?

nodes.name: Legal classification of crypto-asset
nodes.question: Under which regulatory category does the crypto-asset fall: security or financial instrument, stable-value token, fund unit, or other crypto-asset?

nodes.name: Payment stablecoin / e-money / ART regulatory class
nodes.question: Which stablecoin category does the stablecoin fall into under the applicable regime?

nodes.name: Hosted versus unhosted (self-hosted) wallet
nodes.question: Who controls the keys or means of access to the crypto-asset: a service provider, or the user directly?

nodes.name: Wallet storage mode (hot or cold)
nodes.question: Is the wallet's key storage connected to the internet (hot) or offline (cold)?

nodes.name: DLT data structure (blockchain vs non-chain DLT)
nodes.question: Is the distributed ledger organised as a chain of blocks, or by another structure such as a directed acyclic graph?

nodes.name: Ledger access and permissioning
nodes.question: Who may read, write, and maintain consensus on the ledger: anyone, a pre-selected group, or one controlling entity?

nodes.name: Consensus mechanism
nodes.question: By what rule or process is a transaction validated and agreed among DLT nodes?

nodes.name: Finality of agreement
nodes.question: Does the consensus protocol settle transactions deterministically or only probabilistically over time?

nodes.name: Network topology and node roles
nodes.question: How are nodes interconnected and what roles do they hold: decentralised peers, hierarchical tracking and validating nodes, or a central authority?

nodes.name: Smart contract / script language expressiveness
nodes.question: Is the ledger's scripting language Turing-complete, restricted, or supplemented with external data (oracles)?

nodes.name: Smart contract / distributed ledger application scope
nodes.question: Is the software deployed on the ledger a smart contract, application, or protocol, and is its source code publicly available?

nodes.name: Node / DLT network node role
nodes.question: What role does a network node play: full replica holder, partial replica holder, validator, miner, or tracking node?

nodes.name: Ledger scope: open or closed access by design
nodes.question: Is the ledger designed to be open to any network participant or restricted to a closed group for a particular purpose?

nodes.name: Governance model of a DLT system
nodes.question: Who sets and changes the rules of the ledger: an open-source community, a single company, an industry alliance, or a rules-based decentralised governance system?

nodes.name: Software architecture (monolithic vs polylithic)
nodes.question: Is the ledger built as a single integrated application or with decoupled consensus and application layers?

nodes.name: Source code openness
nodes.question: Is the ledger's source code publicly available under an open licence, or closed?

nodes.name: Identity layer and onboarding
nodes.question: Does the ledger verify participant identity through KYC/AML-compliant onboarding, or does it provide no identity layer?

nodes.name: Privacy and anonymity features
nodes.question: Does the ledger or asset obfuscate transaction information, and is that obfuscation built in or added on?

nodes.name: Ledger storage model (what is stored on chain)
nodes.question: What data does the ledger store: full transactions, user balances, or account states, and in what block structure?

nodes.name: Interoperability and intraoperability
nodes.question: Can the ledger exchange information with external systems (interoperability) or other blockchains (intraoperability), and by implicit or explicit means?

nodes.name: Asset supply management (monetary policy)
nodes.question: How is the total supply of the native asset determined: capped, unlimited, or pre-mined?

nodes.name: Native asset presence and type
nodes.question: Does the system have a native asset, and if so is it single, multiple or convertible?

nodes.name: Transaction fee regime
nodes.question: Are fees optional, mandatory or absent, and are they variable with transaction size or fixed per request?

nodes.name: Validator reward mechanism
nodes.question: How are validators rewarded: by a fixed lump-sum block reward, or by block plus security/cross-validation rewards?

nodes.name: Staking arrangement (self, delegated, custodial, liquid)
nodes.question: Who stakes the tokens and operates the validator: the owner, a delegate, a custodian, or through a liquid staking receipt?

nodes.name: Trading venue type
nodes.question: Is the platform a centralised exchange, decentralised exchange, broker-dealer, or peer-to-peer venue?

nodes.name: Principal or agent role in transaction
nodes.question: Does the actor trade or transact as principal (for its own account) or as agent (for a client)?

nodes.name: Crypto-asset service provider or VASP status
nodes.question: Is the actor a regulated provider of crypto-asset services (CASP, VASP, MSB, or intermediary), and within which category?

nodes.name: Crypto-asset service type
nodes.question: Which specified service is the actor providing: custody, trading platform operation, exchange, transfer, execution, placement, advice or portfolio management?

nodes.name: Pooled investment vehicle structure
nodes.question: Is the arrangement a pooled investment vehicle such as a commodity pool, investment company or AIF?

nodes.name: Ecosystem participant role
nodes.question: What is the participant's role in the digital asset ecosystem: issuer, developer, validator, holder, trader, infrastructure provider or other?

nodes.name: Infrastructure provider type
nodes.question: Does the actor supply ancillary technical infrastructure (oracles, bridges, node providers, data providers, auditors) rather than a covered financial service?

nodes.name: Custody model
nodes.question: Who holds the crypto-asset or the means of access (keys): the holder, a custodian, or a multi-party arrangement?

nodes.name: Stablecoin issuer model
nodes.question: Who issues and redeems the stablecoin, and is the issuer a regulated financial institution, bank subsidiary, or nonbank?

nodes.name: Operator of crypto-asset arrangement
nodes.question: Is there a single administrative authority operating the cryptoasset arrangement (issuing, establishing rules, maintaining a ledger, redeeming)?

nodes.name: Control or sufficient influence over DeFi arrangement
nodes.question: Does an identifiable person maintain control or sufficient influence over the DeFi arrangement (through keys, parameters, profit, or shut-down ability)?

nodes.name: Offshore VASP status (activity-based or location-based)
nodes.question: Is the VASP incorporated or physically located outside the jurisdiction where it serves customers, and does it fall within activity-based licensing?

nodes.name: Peer-to-peer (P2P) transaction
nodes.question: Is the transfer conducted directly between users without involvement of a regulated intermediary?

nodes.name: Transfer of crypto-assets (travel rule scope)
nodes.question: Is the transaction a transfer of crypto-assets moving between distributed ledger addresses on behalf of an originator or beneficiary?

nodes.name: Payment service and funds transfer
nodes.question: Is the transaction a transfer of funds through a payment service provider, such as a credit transfer, direct debit or money remittance?

nodes.name: Convertible virtual currency (CVC) status
nodes.question: Is the virtual currency convertible, i.e. does it have an equivalent value to currency or act as a substitute for currency?

nodes.name: Money transmission (acceptance and transmission of value)
nodes.question: Does the actor accept value from one person and transmit it to another, such that it is a money transmission service?

nodes.name: Offer and issuance method (token distribution)
nodes.question: How is the crypto-asset issued or distributed to purchasers: public offer, ICO, airdrop, fork, pre-mine, or end-user distribution?

nodes.name: Minting mechanism
nodes.question: How are new units of the crypto-asset created: consensus rewards, collateral lock-and-mint, staking, wrapping, algorithmic burn-and-mint, governance emission, pre-mining, or NFT registry?

nodes.name: Redemption and reserve adequacy
nodes.question: Are the reserve assets sufficient and redeemable at all times at the peg value, with redemption rights legally enforceable?

nodes.name: Yield or interest on stablecoin
nodes.question: Is the stablecoin yield-bearing or prohibited from paying interest or yield to holders?

nodes.name: Safeguarding and custody obligation
nodes.question: Is the actor safeguarding crypto-assets on behalf of another, and so subject to custody obligations?

nodes.name: Anti-money laundering obligations
nodes.question: Are the AML/CFT obligations attached to the actor or asset, and in which category of obliged entity does the actor fall?

nodes.name: Anonymity-enhancing crypto-asset status
nodes.question: Does the crypto-asset have built-in features that conceal transfer information, and so attract enhanced AML treatment?

nodes.name: Freezing and blocking capability
nodes.question: Does the asset or issuer have the technical capacity to freeze, block or burn units in response to lawful orders?

nodes.name: ICT and operational resilience risk
nodes.question: Is the entity an ICT third-party or financial entity subject to digital operational resilience requirements and critical-function criteria?

nodes.name: Settlement finality and legal enforceability
nodes.question: Are the rights, obligations and settlement finality of the crypto-asset arrangement clearly defined and legally enforceable in all relevant jurisdictions?

nodes.name: Prudential classification group (Basel)
nodes.question: Which Basel prudential group does the cryptoasset exposure fall into: Group 1a, 1b, 2a or 2b?

nodes.name: Traditional finance analogue
nodes.question: Which traditional financial instrument does the crypto-asset's design most closely resemble (commodity, depositary receipt, pass-through certificate, repo, payment in kind, capitalising share class, voting equity)?

nodes.name: Investment contract (Howey) criteria
nodes.question: Does the arrangement involve an investment of money in a common enterprise with an expectation of profits from others' efforts?

nodes.name: Security status of digital asset (US exclusions)
nodes.question: Is the digital asset a security, or excluded from security status by a statutory exclusion (e.g. digital commodity, permitted stablecoin, adjudicated non-security)?

nodes.name: MiFID financial instrument status
nodes.question: Does the crypto-asset qualify as a financial instrument under MiFID II (transferable security, fund unit, derivative, or other Annex I class)?

nodes.name: Excluded instrument category (EU scope exclusions)
nodes.question: Does the crypto-asset fall within an excluded category (deposit, fund, insurance, pension, securitisation, or the ECB/public bodies) that takes it out of MiCA?

nodes.name: Central bank digital currency status
nodes.question: Is the digital money a liability of a central bank denominated in the national unit of account, rather than a private crypto-asset?

nodes.name: Recording and cryptographic linkage
nodes.question: Is the asset recorded on a cryptographically secured distributed ledger, and does cryptography link the data to maintain ledger integrity?

nodes.name: Virtual assets as property or proceeds of crime
nodes.question: Are virtual assets treated as property, proceeds or funds for the purposes of criminal law, freezing or confiscation?

nodes.name: Serious crime threshold for predicate offences
nodes.question: Does the offence meet the threshold of a serious crime (maximum deprivation of liberty of at least four years) for cybercrime and proceeds-of-crime purposes?

nodes.name: Information and communications technology system
nodes.question: Does the device or group of interconnected devices perform automatic processing of electronic or computer data under a program?

nodes.name: Data classification (traffic, content, subscriber)
nodes.question: Does the electronic data concern communication origin, route and time (traffic), its substance (content), or subscriber identity (subscriber information)?

nodes.name: Address linkage to service provider
nodes.question: Is the distributed ledger address linked to a crypto-asset service provider (or equivalent third-country entity), or to no provider?

nodes.name: Originator and beneficiary role
nodes.question: In a transfer of crypto-assets, is the actor the originator (sending) or the beneficiary (receiving) party?

nodes.name: Consumer or retail versus professional user
nodes.question: Is the person acting for purposes outside any trade, business or profession (consumer or retail holder), or on a professional basis?

nodes.name: Related person and affiliated person status
nodes.question: Is the person a founder, executive, large holder or insider of the digital asset issuer, and so connected for disclosure or classification purposes?

nodes.name: Ancillary asset and network token status
nodes.question: Is the digital asset an ancillary asset (issued by an originator with related persons holding interests) or a network token (value primarily derived from the distributed ledger system)?

nodes.name: Reference currency for stablecoin peg (currency vs other)
nodes.question: Is the currency to which the stablecoin pegs a fiat currency of a particular country, and is it the currency of the referenced jurisdiction?

nodes.name: Illicit finance risk category
nodes.question: Which category of ML/TF/PF or sanctions risk does the crypto-asset activity pose: fraud, terrorist financing, proliferation financing, sanctions evasion, unhosted-wallet P2P risk or regulatory arbitrage?

nodes.name: Exemption from MSB status
nodes.question: Is the person exempt from money services business status by being a bank, a registered securities or futures firm, or by an integral or payment processor exemption?

nodes.name: Financial institution status for AML
nodes.question: Is the entity a credit institution, financial institution, investment firm, or other obliged entity under EU AML law?

nodes.name: Tax reporting obligation status (CARF)
nodes.question: Is the cryptoasset service provider subject to crypto-asset reporting and due diligence rules for a given calendar year, and has it notified HMRC?

nodes.name: Jurisdictional regime and home or host state
nodes.question: Which jurisdiction is the home or host state for licensing and supervision, based on registered office, branch or where services are offered?

nodes.name: Validator operation capacity (who may run a node)
nodes.question: Who is authorised or able to operate a validator or node: any participant, a pre-selected set, or a central authority?

nodes.name: Permitted control over client assets (unilateral vs multi-party control)
nodes.question: Can one party unilaterally move the crypto-asset, or does moving it require the approval of multiple keys or parties?

nodes.name: Public offer or private placement
nodes.question: Is the crypto-asset offered to the public broadly, or privately to a defined group of investors?

nodes.name: Nexus to jurisdiction (services offered in jurisdiction)
nodes.question: Are services offered to customers, users or clients in a given jurisdiction, such that licensing or AML obligations apply there?

nodes.name: Privacy mechanism family
nodes.question: Which cryptographic or structural technique provides the privacy or confidentiality guarantee?

nodes.name: smart_contract_deployment_context
nodes.question: In what application context is the smart contract or script deployed?

nodes.name: smart_contract_usage_domain
nodes.question: What application domain or function is the smart contract or ledger application designed to serve?

nodes.name: identity_binding_mechanism
nodes.question: How is a participant's identity bound to the ledger entry?

nodes.name: ledger purpose
nodes.question: What is the primary purpose for which the distributed ledger is used?

nodes.name: ledger partitioning or layering topology
nodes.question: Is the ledger a single chain, multiple parallel or layered chains, or partitioned into sub-ledgers?

candidate_values.definition: Ledger identity is assigned to devices, things or digital twins rather than to human participants.

candidate_values.value: blockchain used for record-keeping of non-asset data
candidate_values.definition: Distributed ledger used to store records, logs, certificates or events rather than a transferable asset or token.
